Sorry, but this is more than I'm willing to take the time to do. If you identify a problem in my code, I'll try to fix it, but I'm not able to take the time to try to debug your code.

I'd suggest using maxmarg() to grab all genotypes on a chromosome and then afterwards finding the particularly positions that you want, rather than looping through the positions and calling maxmarg() repeatedly.

karl

On Friday, June 12, 2020 at 7:47:26 PM UTC-5, Harry C. wrote:
Hi Karl,

I would like to be able to retrieve the most probable genotypes for all individuals at given positions. I have written the attached code:
  • sQTL_table2 is a list containing dataframes with snp names as rows (each snp repeated for once each individual), chromosome/positions/affected protein/genotype as columns)
  • fpr is the fst genoprob
  • DO is the cross2 object

```{r}

cl <- makeCluster(cores) # Create parallel cluster
    registerDoParallel(cl)

g <- foreach(i = 1:length(sQTL_table2)) %dopar% {
       
        this_data <- sQTL_table2[[i]] # Split for parallelisation
       
        geno <- c() # Space to record the genotypes
       
        for(j in 1:(nrow(this_data)/n_inds)){ # Maxmarg collects data for all individuals, so only test each snp once
           
                g_temp <- c() # Genotype of each snp
                g_temp <- qtl2::maxmarg(probs = fpr,
                                        map = DO$pmap,
                                        minprob = 0.9,
                                        chr = this_data$chr[j*n_inds], # Multiply by n_inds so that each snp sampled only once - needed because each snp repeated for each ind
                                        pos = this_data$position[j*n_inds],
                                        return_char = TRUE)
                g_temp <- unname(g_temp)
               
                geno <- c(geno, g_temp) # Add previous SNP genotypes together
           
        }
       
        return(geno)
     
    }

    stopCluster(cl)

```

When I run the code without using multiple cores it works fine, although when I have multiple cores it returns the following error: Error in { : task 1 failed - "map doesn't contain all of the necessary chromosomes".

I checked through the maxmarg code and the condition which triggers this message appears to be:


if (length(map) != length(probs) || !all(names(map) ==
            names(probs))) {
            chr <- names(probs)
            if (!all(chr %in% names(map)))
                stop("map doesn't contain all of the necessary chromosomes")
            map <- map[chr]
        }


Strangely, checking these conditions manually shows that there shouldn't be an issue (lengths are the same for fpr and DO$pmap, and both have identical names).

Would you please be able to help with identifying what might be causing this error? Your help would be greatly appreciated.

Kind regards,

Harry
